channel.title: Chaotic Good Computing
channel.description: Last 40 notes on Chaotic Good Computing

item.title: Working with Valves: Understanding the Structure of "Flat" Organizations
item.description: Many an engineer has heard tales of Valve's "flat" organization structure — what is fact, what is fiction, and how does it actually work? An annotated copy of the 2012 First Edition of Valve's Employee Handbook. (23 min read)

item.title: The Theory of Stupidity (and the graph inside you)
item.description: Our lives are all dominated by a little graph in our hearts — and sometimes, that graph gets wacky. A review of Dietrich Bonhoeffer's "Theory of Stupidity", part of his larger ~1943-1945 work "Letters and Papers from Prison." (12 min read)

item.title: Systems: Week 11
item.description: Watch a human cope about bots taking his job in real time. Is he cooked? Find out tonight in Season of Systems: Week 11! (6 min read)

item.title: Design of a mucin-selective protease for targeted degradation of cancer-associated mucins
item.description: The rubber hits the road on ColabFold! I hope that's rubber I'm smelling — although it may be the computer. A replication attempt of a protein fold figure in K. Pedram et al (2023). (8 min read)

item.title: An Annotated Guide to Hobbyist Protein Folding
item.description: Amaze (or bore) your friends and family by picking up on a hot new hobby that's all the rage — protein folding! An annotated starter to the 2021 paper "ColabFold - Making protein folding accessible to all" (10 min read)

item.title: Agentic Programming as Theory Building
item.description: Do humans have a role in software development anymore? Absolutely — but we need to rethink what it means to program. An modern review of Peter Naur's 1985 essay "Programming as Theory Building" (40 min read)

item.title: APL: Pattern 4; Agricultural Valleys
item.description: Urban development has the high ground over agricultural and ecological preservation — and it should! *A Pattern Language* annotations on Pattern 4: Agricultural Valleys (2 min read)

item.title: APL: Pattern 5; Lace of Country Streets
item.description: How dense is too dense? How sparse is too sparse? Annotations for A Pattern Language's proposals for the density of metro-adjacent country streets for agriculture, recreation, and preservation. (3 min read)

item.title: APL: Pattern 1; Independent Regions
item.description: Home isn't where the heart is — it's a single node on a very, very large graph. Annotations for the "Independent Regions" pattern of *A Pattern Language*. (10 min read)

item.title: APL: Pattern 2; The Distribution of Towns
item.description: How close is too close? How far is too far? *A Pattern Language* annotations related to the statistical, economic, and ecologic concerns in balancing how dense human habitats ought to be. (5 min read)

item.title: APL: Pattern 3; City Country Fingers
item.description: City, with natural stripes — or nature, with city stripes? Annotations for A Pattern Language, and tracking public opinion of where Americans want to live over the past 50 years. (4 min read)

item.title: APL: Pattern 0; Introduction
item.description: Can graphs be libertarian? Authoritarian? Annotations for the introductory portion of the 1977 book A Pattern Language. (9 min read)

item.title: Ants in the Neighborhood
item.description: Is Jane Street run by soccer-loving ants? Inconclusive. We *can* conclude that they're fans of Markov Chains, though — an invaluable tool for understanding complex data structures. (1 min read)

item.title: A Pattern Language, and a Beautiful Day in the Neighborhood
item.description: The beginning of a topological review of the 1977 urban design and architecture reference book A Pattern Language, and a journey to understand Earth's greatest graph: the Earth, itself. (12 min read)

item.title: Evolution and Revolution as Organizations Grow
item.description: Annotations for Greiner's 1972 paper "Evolution and Revolution as Organizations Grow", about the structural composition of organizations at different sizes and requirements. (16 min read)

item.title: Quick Fix: Tone Down Obsidian List/Header Padding
item.description: Annoyed by Obsidian Live Preview over-padding headers and aggressively indenting? Some snippets to help keep your notes from jumping around, so you can focus on actually writing them. (3 min read)

item.title: The Advantages of Advantage: Intro to Probability Convolutions
item.description: What *is* the advantage of rolling with advantage? Exploring dice roll combinations and probability convolutions. (8 min read)

item.title: Dice Roll Distribution Widget
item.description: Discover the probability distributions of different dice roll combinations (1 min read)

item.title: Quartz Widgets: Graphs, Galore!
item.description: I killed 4 of my blogs trying to implement MDX support. Will this one be next? Using MDX with Quartz to create interactive graphs, diagrams, and demos — clear as day. (9 min read)

item.title: LLMs; or, How to Run Your Own Hostage Negotiation
item.description: LLMs: Are we doomed to die, or born to garden? I'd like to make the case that AI is less like Terminator, and more like tomatoes. (8 min read)

item.title: Intro to Event Storming
item.description: Notes from learning Event Storming for domain-driven design. Thoughts on phases, color-coded chaos, and how to transition from fast pitches to full products. (6 min read)

item.title: Kickoff: Season of Systems
item.description: I'm learning to live with the systems that stole my beloved em-dash. A season dedicated to negotiating how to live with the agentic models that have turned my career upside-down. (8 min read)

item.title: Review: Season of Rhythm
item.description: Looking back at my year-long attempt to build up long-lasting habits. A retrospective on routines, remote work transitions, and learning the art of slow-and-steady. (7 min read)

item.title: LLMs: A Primer Presentation for Our Newest, Scariest Tool
item.description: An engineer-focused primer on the mechanisms that drive Large Language Models. Basics on how we got here, how they work, and how to use them without feeling an apocalyptic dread. (1 min read)

item.title: Typst Resume Template
item.description: A beginner-friendly resume template in Typst — 100% less LaTeX, 100% more opinions. (38 min read)

item.title: Terraform LocalStack Testing

item.title: The Simple Economics of Open Source
item.description: Why do we do what we do? "Egoboo." Exploring economic models of OSS contributions beyond altruism and ego. (15 min read)

item.title: College Admissions and the Stability of Marriage
item.description: A dive into the hottest algorithm of the 1960s: Gale-Shapley matchmaking. Who knew that the mysteries of the heart could be solved with a matrix? (6 min read)

item.title: Feeling Right, Nothing Done: Don't Be the Death of Consensus
item.description: Classifying opinions as "strong" or "weak" to stop wasting hours in fruitless engineering debates. How consensus can beat being "right", and an open letter for the tactically apathetic. (7 min read)

item.title: Before You Slabtop Your Laptop: A Brief Warning
item.description: PSA: Check if your laptop needs an LCD for POST before removing the screen. Learned this the hard way after 5 hours and a fried motherboard. Learn from my dumb mistakes. (2 min read)

item.title: GPTinglish: Unnatural Language Processing
item.description: The only market crashing is the market for sanitized language. Stay human. Embrace typos. (7 min read)

item.title: Turning SelfControl into Self Restraint
item.description: Building a Raycast plugin to schedule website blocks — because checking news "just one more time" destroys flow. Automate SelfControl and self control: take your laptop back. (4 min read)

item.title: Caveat Lector: Reader Beware
item.description: I'm embracing being wrong on the internet in an effort to learn in public. A disclaimer on digital gardening, dead pixels, and the fear of terminal online-ness. (3 min read)

item.title: The Quest to Slay The Goblin
item.description: My life devolves into sleep-eat-procrastinate cycles without structure—I call this "The Goblin." Productivity tools, hating on hustle culture, and a new definition for horticulture. (2 min read)
